audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Renekton the first-item and 2+-item rows and the page called it a 'Favoured matchup' at difficulty 4/10, while the win rate is 49.14% over 1457 games and the page's own whys[5]/[6] say the 1v1 is over once his Sheen item lands.
audit.why: Nasus scales infinitely; carry threat is already listed 10/10. A chart that hands Renekton the late rows tells a paying player to keep taking a side-lane duel the same page says he loses.
audit.corrected: Level 3 -> Skill (whys[2] already says trades go even), First item and 2+ items -> Nasus, ratings lowered to match, difficulty 4/10 -> 5/10, and the rating line reads 'Even matchup'.

audit.why: Spikes are already concrete and correct: level 2 pre-Wither all-in, level 6 Dominus, his Sheen item, 300+ stacks. Wither's 15s rank-1 cooldown is given in whys[3] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interactions were absent. (a) Wither's attack-speed component starves Fury generation, so a Withered Renekton's follow-up W is the bare 0.75s stun, not the empowered 1.5s one — but under Dominus, Fury ticks on a timer, so Wither stops starving it. (b) Fury of the Sands grants Nasus bonus Armor and Magic Resistance and deals percent-health damage, and empowered Slice and Dice reduces Armor, which is the direct answer.
audit.why: Renekton's Fury comes from attacks (kit: 'Renekton's attacks generate Fury'), so cutting attack speed cuts Fury; Dominus states 'While in this form, Renekton gains Fury periodically', which bypasses that. Fury of the Sands text lists bonus Armor and Magic Resistance and carries the percentHealth flag — the missingInteractions file flags resistances-invalidated for exactly this matchup.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now says Dominus is the answer to Wither because Fury ticks on a timer; wants.foe[0] states the Fury-starve consequence in stun-duration terms; dosFull[2] points empowered E at the bonus armour his R hands him.

edits.after: Dominus is the answer to Wither: Fury ticks on a timer under it, so the slow no longer starves your Fury and empowered W stays available.

edits.after: Hit Wither as you dash in — the attack-speed cut starves your Fury, so your W stuns 0.75s not 1.5s

edits.before: Nasus wastes Wither — commit the full pattern immediately.

notes: Level 6 was left as 'Skill' in both layers rather than following the packet's 'Nasus': the rewritten whys[4] now explains that Dominus' timer-based Fury generation defeats the Wither Fury-starve, which is a genuine Renekton advantage at 6, so handing the row outright to Nasus would contradict the page's own mid text and spikes[1]. Rows 3, 6 and 7 were proposed as matched full/content pairs. Unwritten but true and worth a future pass: Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell.
